newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand sees big potential for firms in India.
newsitem.headline: Thailand sees big potential for firms in India.

text.p: Thailand sees much business potential in India after New Delhi's latest budget, Thai Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee said on Monday.
"India's new budget showed that the country is serious on economic reform which will make it easier for investors to do business there. It is very encouraging," he told reporters.
"This budget will make India both our important business partner and competitor ... And given the size of her market, there is a lot of potential," Narongchai said on his return from a trip to India.
India's budget, presented at the end of February, slashed personal and corporate taxes and ushered in other key incentives to investors.
Narongchai said Thai exports and investments in processed food, petrochemical and autoparts could do well in that country and more major Thai firms were keen on moving there.
Thai Petrochemical Industry, for example, had held talks with Indian companies to set up a three million tonne iron ore pelletisation plant, oil refineries and a petrochemical plant there.
"Current total trade between Thailand and India amounts to only US$1 billion a year ... But I can see that improving with the more open economy India is offering," Narongchai said.
